# Antonio P. Sberna

> Research fellow in Structural Engineering at the University of Chieti-Pescara (Italy). Research on earthquake engineering: seismic retrofitting of existing structures, performance-based earthquake engineering, reduced-order modelling, regional-scale seismic risk; more recently, agentic workflows for structural engineering.

Personal academic website: research, publications, activities and a blog of opinion essays on research in the age of AI agents. Blog posts are also available as clean Markdown (the links below), with margin notes as footnotes and later additions as dated "Update" sections.

Agents reading this site on behalf of a person are welcome. Automated collection for training models is not permitted (see https://AntonioSberna.github.io/robots.txt). Texts and original images are licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://AntonioSberna.github.io/license/): please attribute to Antonio P. Sberna and link the page.

## Blog posts

- [A Gym for Theory](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/blog/2026-llm-theory-gym/index.md): If agents are becoming the workforce of intellectual professions, what remains is theory, and the question of where to train it. (24 October 2026)
- [Why Not Straight to Assembly?](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/blog/2026-why-not-assembly/index.md): Ask an LLM for something computational and you get Python back. Why not something closer to the metal? I asked one. (21 October 2026)
- [These Are All English Words](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/blog/2026-on-thinking-differently-screen/index.md): I no longer write code with my hands, and I no longer google. Notes from a millennial on a shift that will not be reversed. (17 October 2026)
- [Who Else Read My Proposal?](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/blog/2026-llm-privacy/index.md): Almost every grant proposal this year has probably passed through an LLM running on someone else's server. Three loosely connected thoughts on what that means. (4 October 2026; updated 10 November 2026)
- [The Elephant in the Session Room](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/blog/2026-ecee-science-w-agents/index.md): Five days in Berlin for ECEE 2026, and what lingers is not a talk but a feeling of unease. Not because of the science: the science was excellent. Professor … (26 September 2026; updated 8 November 2026)

## Research

- [My research in plain words](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/research/): What Antonio P. Sberna studies, explained without the jargon: earthquakes, existing buildings and how to make them safer.
- [Influence of Bedrock Seismic Action Modelling on Microzonation](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/influence-of-bedrock-seismic-action-modelling-on-microzonation/): Manuscript under review (Buildings). To predict how shaking will vary across a town, engineers first need realistic earthquake motions for the deep rock beneath it. Using the town of Norcia and the 2016 Central Italy earthquake as a test, this study shows that motions generated on a computer can match real measurements more closely than the usual approach of scaling up past earthquakes.
- [Closed-form biaxial curvature and ductility domains for reinforced concrete rectangular sections](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/closed-form-biaxial-curvature-and-ductility-domains-for-reinforced-concrete-rectangular-sections/): Manuscript under review (Engineering Structures). In an earthquake, a concrete column can bend in any direction, and how far it can bend before failing depends on that direction. Using a large set of simulated column sections and machine learning, this study derives compact formulas that engineers can use directly in their analysis and design tools.
- [Near-Base Lateral Impact Response of Circular Concrete-Filled Steel Tube Bridge-Pier Columns: Experimental Comparison of Cantilever and Propped-Cantilever Boundary Conditions](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/near-base-lateral-impact-response-of-circular-concrete-filled-steel-tube-bridge-pier-columns-experimental-comparison-of-cantilever-and-propped-cantilever-boundary-conditions/): Manuscript under review (Engineering Structures). What happens when a bridge pier is hit near its base, as in a collision with a vehicle? Scale-model columns made of steel tubes filled with concrete were struck by a hammer in the laboratory, with and without a support at the top. The support reduced the maximum sideways movement by 28-41%, but concentrated the damage near the point of impact.
- [Characterizing bamboo aggregate foamed concrete for sustainable construction: thermal, acoustic, mechanical, and environmental aspects](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/characterizing-bamboo-aggregate-foamed-concrete-for-sustainable-construction-thermal-acoustic-mechanical-and-environmental-aspects/): Materials and Structures, 2026. Can waste from bamboo manufacturing make concrete greener? This study replaces part of the sand in a lightweight foamed concrete with recycled bamboo, and tests its strength, its heat and sound performance, and its environmental impact. The result is a promising low-density material that insulates better against heat.
- [Enhancing seismic site response analyses: tuning soil properties via genetic algorithms and Bayesian model updating from downhole array data](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/enhancing-seismic-site-response-analyses-tuning-soil-properties-via-genetic-algorithms-and-bayesian-model-updating-from-downhole-array-data/): Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering, 2026. The ground under a building can change how an earthquake is felt at the surface. This study uses records from instruments placed below ground to fine-tune a computer model of the soil, and to measure how much uncertainty remains, for more reliable predictions of the shaking.
- [Local Shear Demand Correction Model for the Analysis of Infilled Frames Using Equivalent Struts](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/local-shear-demand-correction-model-for-the-analysis-of-infilled-frames-using-equivalent-struts/): Journal of Structural Engineering, 2025. During an earthquake, the masonry walls inside a concrete frame push against the columns and add extra force at their ends. This study provides a straightforward correction that lets engineers estimate this force while still using simple building models.
- [Enhanced Compressive Performance and Energy Absorption in SLM-Fabricated 316L Arrowhead Auxetics via Tendon and Stuffer Geometry Modification](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/enhanced-compressive-performance-and-energy-absorption-in-slm-fabricated-316l-arrowhead-auxetics-via-tendon-and-stuffer-geometry-modification/): Composite Structures, 2025. Most materials get thinner when stretched, but auxetic structures do the opposite. This study 3D-prints stainless-steel lattices of this kind and adjusts their geometry so that they absorb more energy when crushed, which is useful for protective applications.
- [Reliability-based seismic retrofitting design methodology for non-ductile reinforced concrete frame structures](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/reliability-based-seismic-retrofitting-design-methodology-for-non-ductile-reinforced-concrete-frame-structures/): Probabilistic Engineering Mechanics, 2025. Instead of only asking whether an older building passes a safety check, this method estimates how rarely earthquakes would push it past given levels of damage, including collapse. It then looks for the strengthening solutions that meet the target at the lowest cost.
- [Engineered frameworks for sustainable seismic retrofitting design: a state-of-the-art review](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/engineered-frameworks-for-sustainable-seismic-retrofitting-design-a-state-of-the-art-review/): Bulletin of Earthquake Engineering, 2025. Strengthening a building against earthquakes is often designed through experience and trial and error. This review surveys more structured methods that also weigh costs and environmental and social impacts, compares their strengths and limits, and points out what research still has to solve.
- [Structural health monitoring of masonry structures using stress sensors: Experimental induced damage tests and proposed approach for real-time monitoring](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/structural-health-monitoring-of-masonry-structures-using-stress-sensors-experimental-induced-damage-tests-and-proposed-approach-for-real-time-monitoring/): Construction and Building Materials, 2024. Can a masonry building tell us when it is getting damaged? Small sensors were placed in the mortar of test walls, which were then deliberately damaged in the laboratory, to develop an approach for monitoring a structure's health in real time.
- [Cost-effective topology optimization of masonry structure reinforcements by a linear static analysis-based GA framework](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/cost-effective-topology-optimization-of-masonry-structure-reinforcements-by-a-linear-static-analysis-based-ga-framework/): Bulletin of Earthquake Engineering, 2024. Many existing buildings stand on masonry walls with no reinforcement, which makes them vulnerable to earthquakes. This study presents a computer method that chooses which walls to strengthen with reinforced plaster, so that the building passes its safety checks at the lowest cost.
- [Dynamic progressive collapse response of multi-storey frame structures with masonry infills](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/dynamic-progressive-collapse-response-of-multi-storey-frame-structures-with-masonry-infills/): Structures, 2023. If a column of a concrete building is suddenly lost, can the rest of the structure hold, or does the collapse spread? This study looks at how the masonry walls inside the frame influence the outcome.
- [A genetic algorithm-based framework for seismic retrofitting cost and expected annual loss optimization of non-conforming reinforced concrete frame structures](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/a-genetic-algorithm-based-framework-for-seismic-retrofitting-cost-and-expected-annual-loss-optimization-of-non-conforming-reinforced-concrete-frame-structures/): Computers and Structures, 2022. Strengthening a building costs money today, but earthquake damage costs money in the future too. This study uses artificial intelligence to find strengthening solutions that are cheap to build and also keep the expected yearly cost of damage under control.
- [A new empirical formulation for the out-of-plane resistance of masonry infills in reinforced concrete frames](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/a-new-empirical-formulation-for-the-out-of-plane-resistance-of-masonry-infills-in-reinforced-concrete-frames/): Engineering Structures, 2022. The masonry walls that fill the frames of concrete buildings can be pushed outwards by an earthquake. This study offers a simple formula, based on laboratory tests and computer simulations, to estimate how strong these walls are against that push.
- [A new genetic algorithm-based framework for optimized design of steel-jacketing retrofitting in shear-critical and ductility-critical RC frame structures](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/a-new-genetic-algorithm-based-framework-for-optimized-design-of-steel-jacketing-retrofitting-in-shear-critical-and-ductility-critical-rc-frame-structures/): Engineering Structures, 2021. Old concrete columns can fail in an earthquake in different ways, some more sudden than others. This study improves a computer method that finds the cheapest way to strengthen them with steel, whichever kind of weakness they have.
- [Optimal seismic retrofitting of reinforced concrete buildings by steel-jacketing using a genetic algorithm-based framework](https://AntonioSberna.github.io/papers/optimal-seismic-retrofitting-of-reinforced-concrete-buildings-by-steel-jacketing-using-a-genetic-algorithm-based-framework/): Engineering Structures, 2020. Many older concrete buildings were not designed for earthquakes, and strengthening them is expensive. This study uses a computer method inspired by natural evolution to work out which columns need steel reinforcement, and how much, so that safety is reached at a lower cost.
